situation: Aïcha travels by bus from Garoua to Ngaoundéré. On a long, straight road, she sees a big lorry coming from far away. At first, she sees only the top of the lorry. Then, little by little, she sees the whole lorry.
Her little brother says, "The Earth is flat like a table." Aïcha thinks that the lorry appeared little by little because the Earth is round, but she cannot explain it well.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Aïcha cannot explain how the lorry shows that the Earth is round.
Which part of the lorry did Aïcha see first?
She saw the top of the lorry first, and then the rest of the lorry.
How can Aïcha convince her brother that the Earth is not flat?
She can show him a globe and photos of the Earth taken from space, and explain the example of the lorry or of a ship at sea.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to know the true size and shape of our planet, and to prove its shape with simple observations.

qa.q: Study the size of the Earth.
What is the distance around the Earth at the Equator?
qa.a: The distance around the Earth at the Equator (the equatorial circumference) is about 40,075 km.

qa.q: Compare the equatorial diameter and the polar diameter. What do you notice?
qa.a: The equatorial diameter (12,756 km) is about 42 km longer than the polar diameter (12,714 km). The Earth is wider at the Equator.

sum.title: I. Size of the Earth
sum.intro: The Earth is a very large planet. Its main measurements are the following:
items: – The radius of the Earth is about 6,370 km.

qa.q: The Earth is not a perfect ball. Where is it flattened, and where does it bulge?
qa.a: It is slightly flattened at the North Pole and the South Pole, and it bulges (is wider) at the Equator.

qa.q: What is the name of this true shape of the Earth?
qa.a: This shape is called an oblate spheroid (or geoid). It is caused by the rotation of the Earth.

sum.title: II. Shape of the Earth
defs: An oblate spheroid is a sphere that is slightly flattened at the poles and slightly bulging at the Equator.
items: The Earth is almost a sphere, but its true shape is an oblate spheroid. The bulge at the Equator is caused by the rotation of the Earth.

qa.title: Question 1
qa.q: A ship sails away from the coast. Which part disappears first? Why?
qa.a: The hull (bottom) disappears first and the mast (top) last, because the ship moves over the curved surface of the Earth.

qa.q: During an eclipse of the Moon, what is the shape of the shadow of the Earth on the Moon?
qa.a: The shadow of the Earth is always round (curved). Only a sphere gives a round shadow from every side.

qa.q: Why does the Sun rise in Maroua a few minutes before it rises in Douala?
qa.a: Maroua is further east than Douala. On a round, turning Earth, the Sun rises first in the east and later in the west.

qa.q: Give two other proofs that the Earth is round.
qa.a: People can travel around the world and return to their starting point. Photos from satellites and astronauts show a round Earth.

sum.title: III. Proofs of the Shape of the Earth
sum.intro: Many observations prove that the Earth is round:
items: When a ship sails away, its hull disappears first and its mast last. It moves over the curve of the Earth.
During an eclipse of the Moon, the shadow of the Earth on the Moon is always round.
The Sun rises and sets at different times in different places. It rises first in places further east.
From a mountain or an aeroplane, the horizon looks curved, and we can see further when we go higher.
People can travel around the world in one direction and return to their starting point (circumnavigation).
Photos taken by satellites and astronauts show that the Earth is round.

evaluation: What is the true shape of the Earth?
The true shape of the Earth is an oblate spheroid: flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator.
Why is the equatorial circumference longer than the polar circumference?
It is longer because the Earth bulges at the Equator.
Give three proofs that the Earth is round.
The ship at sea, the round shadow of the Earth during an eclipse of the Moon, and photos from space.
remediation: The Earth is flattened at the ______.
The equatorial circumference is about ______ km.
The true shape of the Earth is an oblate ______.
When a ship sails away, the ______ disappears first.
During an eclipse of the Moon, the shadow of the Earth is ______.
end.homework: Look at the Moon on three different evenings this week. Draw its shape each time and write the date under each drawing.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Further Study 1: The Universe and the Moon.
